entwurf.thema: The origin of Lego from wooden toys to plastic bricks

teile.text: A fire in 1932 destroyed Ole Kirk Christiansen’s wooden toy shop during the Great Depression.
teile.szene: A carpenter in a smoky Danish workshop watches sparks rise from a workbench, painted open-world game poster style with bold ink contours.

teile.text: After the blaze, he shifted focus to plastic bricks, beginning production in Denmark in 1947.
teile.szene: A man carefully assembling small wooden duck toys on a plain wooden table under warm indoor lighting.

teile.text: So what changed that made Lego a global brand?
teile.szene: An industrial machine pressing early red plastic bricks inside a modest mid-century European factory.

teile.text: In 1961 Ole built Billund Airport to aid worldwide exports of his bricks.
teile.szene: A close-up shot of hands clicking two colorful plastic studs together firmly on a bright surface.

teile.text: By 2015 Lego revenue hit US$2.1 billion, surpassing Mattel.
teile.szene: A small prop airplane sitting on a grassy rural airfield with wooden hangars in the background under an open sky.

teile.text: In May 2025 the company moved its North American headquarters to Boston.
teile.szene: A modern warehouse filled with stacked boxes of construction toys under bright overhead lights.

teile.text: Remember the shop that burned—now it fuels a billion-dollar empire; like, share, save.
teile.szene: A neat tower of interlocking red and yellow toy bricks standing upright against a clean neutral background.

entwurf.beschreibung: Discover how Lego transformed from a Depression‑era wooden toy workshop into the world's largest toy company.
